entries.title: Letter triggers no longer fire right after a letter
entries.now: A trigger that starts with a letter fires only at the start of a word: `A uu` gives `A \cup`, but `Auu` stays `Auu`. This is Castel's rule, and the main reason `\subset`, `\approx`, `\emptyset` … now type as written.
entries.alternative: `fire_after_letters = true` in prefs.lua (`latex = { … }`): letter triggers fire after a letter again (`Auu` → `A\cup`), but still never inside a `\command` name. The mangling test passes with either setting.
entries.recommendation: Keep it off (as now). One space before the trigger is all it takes, and two letters typed together in maths stay two letters. Turn it on if your fingers keep typing `Auu`.
entries.side: Suffix snippets are not affected: `xsr` → `x^{2}`, `xhat` → `\hat{x}`, `x2` → `x_{2}`, `Adag` → `A^{\dagger}` still work after a letter. Two knock-on effects: after a letter `xp1` and `he4` now act as a subscript (`Axp1` → `Axp_{1}`), and `Acdot` stays `Acdot`.

entries.title: mk in .tex files: $…$ or \(…\)?
entries.now: `mk` gives `$…$` in .tex and .md files, as before.
entries.alternative: `\(…\)` in .tex files: what LaTeX's own documentation prefers (clearer errors when a `$` goes missing).
entries.recommendation: Keep `$…$`. It's what you type everywhere else, what Castel uses, and Backspace-in-empty-`$|$` and Tab-out-of-`$` are built around it. Nothing breaks either way.
entries.how: To switch: in snippets/tex/text.lua make the mk line `text("mk", function() return vim.bo.filetype == "tex" and [[\(<>\)]] or [[$<>$]] end, "changed")`.

entries.title: Auto subscript only after a single letter or a Greek letter
entries.now: `x2` → `x_{2}`, `ab2` → `ab_{2}`, `\alpha2` → `\alpha_{2}`, but the last letter of any other `\command` no longer gets one: `\leq2` and `\sqrt2` stay as typed.
entries.before_text: The letter could be the end of a command: `\leq2` → `\leq_{2}`, `\sqrt2` → garbage. It also happened to give `log2` → `\log_{2}` and `sin2` → `\sin_{2}`.
entries.alternative: Allow a subscript after a few named commands as well (`\log`, `\lim`, …): one line each in snippets/tex/subscripts.lua.
entries.recommendation: Keep it (as now). For `\log_{2}` type `log_2`: `_` adds the braces.

entries.title: Castel additions: keep all 20?
entries.now: 20 snippets from Castel's set are on (see “New from Castel”): `pi`, `zeta`, `star`, `perp`, `lll`, `mcal`, `DD`, `~~`, `<!`, `<>`, `compl`, select-then-`/`, `lr`/`lrb` with Tab, and `table`, `fig`, `desc`, `pac`, `plot`, `bigfun` with Tab at the start of a line in .tex.
entries.alternative: Veto any of them: delete its line (they are marked `"castel"` at the end of the line).
entries.recommendation: Keep them. None fires while you type ordinary words or commands (tested), and the Tab ones only do something when you press Tab right after the word at the start of a line.

entries.title: Castel's environment snippets for text: add them as Tab snippets?
entries.now: Not added. Castel's `beg`, `enum`, `item`, `ali` fire by themselves at the start of a line in text, so a line starting with “began”, “items”, “enumerate” or “align” would turn into an environment. Your `beg` works in maths only, as before.
entries.alternative: Add them as Tab snippets (start of a line, .tex only), like `table` and `fig`: `item` Tab → `\begin{itemize} \item … \end{itemize}`.
entries.recommendation: Leave them out for now; say so if you write a lot of lists or align environments in .tex and they go in as Tab snippets.

entries.title: No maths snippets inside \ce{…} and \pu{…}
entries.why: mhchem has its own syntax there: `H2O`, `A -> B`, `m2`. The auto subscript used to turn `\ce{H2O}` into `\ce{H_{2}O}` and `\pu{3 m2}` into `\pu{3 m_{2}}`. Labels and references (`\label{}`, `\ref{}`, `\eqref{}`, `\cite{}`) are protected the same way.

entries.title: { right after an automatic _{ is skipped
entries.why: `_` already opens `_{…}`; typing `x_{i}` as written used to give `x_{{i}}`. Now the second `{` is skipped, so both `x_i` and `x_{i}` give `x_{i}`.

entries.title: mk only at the start of a word, and not in comments or `code`
entries.why: `Hellomk` used to give `Hello$…$`; inside `` `code` `` in .md and in a `%` comment in .tex it fired too. Now it needs a space (or line start) before it, like the maths triggers.

entries.title: dm in a list item: no longer fires inside words; indented items line up
entries.why: In a list item, typing a word containing “dm” (admit, landmark) used to start display maths in the middle of the word. Now `dm` has to start a word. In an indented item (`  - …`) the block now lines up with the item's text (LuaSnip keeps the line's indentation).

entries.title: Snippets live in snippets/tex/*.lua, not in ~/.config/latex-suite
entries.why: One Lua file per topic (sets, greek, operations, accents, subscripts, symbols, calculus, trig, environments, brackets, physics, chemistry, text, visual), one snippet per line, loaded by LuaSnip's from_lua loader and reloaded on save. ntex no longer reads ~/.config/latex-suite at all (Superset still does; it is untouched). Space e picks a file; :SnippetReport (Space r) lists what loaded and any error. A file with an error keeps its previous snippets; at startup the other files still load (before, one typo in snippets.js meant no snippets at all).

entries.title: Latex Suite settings moved into prefs.lua (`latex = { … }`), same values
entries.why: Auto-fraction (and its symbol, breaking characters, excluded places), matrix environments, tabout closing symbols, enlarge triggers, auto-delete $, removing trailing spaces in inline maths: all in prefs.lua now, with the values your Obsidian import had. obsidian-settings.json and settings.json are no longer read. `wordDelimiters` is gone: the word-start rule replaces it. `conceal` in prefs.lua is now simply on/off (there is no shared setting to follow).

entries.title: Function snippets are Lua; regex triggers are Lua patterns
entries.why: No JavaScript, no converter, no JSON cache, no jsregexp: `iden3`, the auto subscripts, `\sin` + letter and `dm` in a list are short Lua functions or Lua patterns in the snippet files, visible and editable. Results are identical (see “Kept as is”).

entries.title: Commands renamed; the old names still work
entries.why: :SnippetReport (Space r), :SnippetEdit (Space e, now a picker of the snippet files), :SnippetReload, :Conceal (F2). :LatexSuiteReport, :LatexSuiteEdit, :LatexSuiteReload and :LatexSuiteConceal do the same; delete them from lua/snips/init.lua when you no longer need them.
